fixtureShape: two damaged COPIES of R5's bundle (the bundle itself is never written to): (a) one accepted media file's bytes altered after bundling; (b) manifest.json rewritten with bundleSchema 1.
acceptanceRow: Changed or missing source: damaged bundles are refused; changed media/settings invalidate affected presentation work; unchanged compilation reuses valid work. Relocated outputs retain usable links.
notes: D1: the compiler runs `evalrun.py verify-bundle DIR` first and refuses, by name, schema-unsupported (bundle schema != 2) and bundle-refused (bundle.complete false, defects listed). An altered media file is an evidence row that no longer hashes to its recorded sha256 - verify-bundle's `mismatched` - so bundle.complete is false and the compiler refuses bundle-refused. The refusal name is asserted on the tool's own words with the case directory's name scrubbed out (the directory is named after the damage).

The exit code number is not fixed by D1; non-zero is asserted. Whether a refused plan writes any file is not fixed either; what is asserted is that no presentation.json claiming schemaVersion 1 with integrity ok is written for a refused bundle.

'Unchanged compilation reuses valid work' is measured as D2's determinism (two plans over one unchanged bundle give one presentationId) and 'changed settings invalidate' as a different presentationId under --exhaustive (R3). The reel's per-segment cache (D6 `reused`) is agent B's test_evalreel territory and is not asserted here.

'Relocated outputs retain usable links': `evalreport verify --out MOVED` exits 0 after the whole OUT directory is moved, and the driver's own link check (every [E-]/[M-] token in report.md has an anchor in evidence-index.md, every relative image path exists) holds from the new location.
